title: Entry door declares each action: its seat, its engine claim, its reversal
shared_surfaces: app/api/write-capability-gate.test.ts (repo-wide behavioural door list - append two DOORS rows only)
app/api/route-capability-coverage.test.ts (repo-wide ratchet - delete two ALLOWED lines only)
acceptance: write-capability-gate (real handler, unit-db, signed viewer session): POST /api/pipeline/[id] {action:'reject'} -> 403, body.code 'FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY', body.capability 'pipeline:write'; the entry's status is still 'active' and it has no new pipeline_events row. Owner session on the same call is not refused at the seat (non-vacuity). No session -> 401 (unchanged).

Viewer POST /api/pipeline/[id] {action:'set_notes', notes:'x'} and {action:'reinstate'} -> 403 FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY each, before the body's action runs (the capability is read from the declared table, so every action the door dispatches is covered, not only the three board moves).
Viewer POST /api/pipeline/outcomes {entryId, performance:4} -> 403 FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY; no dev_outcomes row is written. GET /api/pipeline/outcomes stays operator-gated read (not capability-gated).

entry-actions.ts (pure): ENTRY_ACTIONS is a literal table keyed by exactly set_github, set_notes, reinstate, resolve_intake, set_stage, accept, reject, approve_event; every row declares capability 'pipeline:write'; entryActionOf('bogus') -> null and the route answers 400 PIPELINE_ACTION_UNKNOWN; only the 'accept' row declares engineClaim:true.

Engine claim is honoured only where declared: an operator session POSTs {action:'reject', actor:'sim'} on an active entry -> 200, the pipeline_events row is kind 'rejected' (NOT 'auto_rejected'), the sealed decision is kind 'rejected' with a 'human:*' actor, and the entry does NOT appear in listReconsiderQueue. {action:'accept', actor:'sim'} still seals actor 'auto:sim' / kind 'auto_advanced' (the guided sim's only use, useSimulationEngine.ts:260 and useSimulationWalk.ts:575, is unchanged).

Reinstate seals where the candidate really landed: on a workspace whose screened-landing column is renamed, reinstating an auto-rejected entry -> 200 and the sealed 'reinstated' record's inputs.restoredStage equals the returned entry.stage (today the literal 'Screened').

Reinstate refuses a hand reject: an entry whose newest decision event is 'rejected' (a recruiter's reject, not 'auto_rejected') -> 409 PIPELINE_NOT_REINSTATABLE; status stays 'rejected', no 'reinstated' event, no seal - so the record 'Auto-rejection reversed' is only ever written over an auto-rejection.

authz-parity is derived, not hand-listed: the test walks app/api/pipeline/**/route.ts and fails for any exported handler that neither calls requireOperator (plus requireCapabilityCoded('pipeline:write') for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) nor appears in a reasoned allowlist; route-capability-coverage.test.ts ALLOWED no longer contains 'pipeline/[id]/route.ts' or 'pipeline/outcomes/route.ts'.
premise: app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:54-56 - POST's only gate is requireOperator(); the file has no requireCapability/requireCapabilityCoded call anywhere, yet it dispatches reject (candidate-facing rejection comm), accept (which EXTENDS a drafted offer on offer_review, pipeline-entry-action.ts:189 extendDraftedOffer), set_stage and reinstate.

app/api/route-capability-coverage.test.ts:163-164 - 'pipeline/[id]/route.ts' and 'pipeline/outcomes/route.ts' sit in ALLOWED as 'slice 2 candidate - ungated when this ratchet landed; not yet judged', while the sibling doors batch/route.ts:72-73, command/route.ts:60-61, command/reverse/route.ts:25-26, stage-migration/route.ts:56-57, stage-sla/route.ts:41-42 all ask requireCapabilityCoded('pipeline:write').
app/api/pipeline/outcomes/route.ts:90-91 - POST (records an on-the-job judgement about a named hire) is gated by requireOperator only.

app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:68,83,101,135 - four actions are handled by string-compare branches in the route; the rest fall through to runPipelineEntryAction at :147-157. No table names what each action requires; the requirement lives in whichever branch remembered.

app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:154 forwards `actor: body.actor` for EVERY action; pipeline-entry-action.ts:315 `simActor = input.actor === SIM_ACTOR`, :322 sealActor = 'auto:sim', :480 event actor 'system', :500 seal kind 'auto_rejected' for a reject. db/pipeline.ts:3087-3088: actor 'system' makes the event kind auto_rejected. So any operator session can file a human reject as a machine auto-reject, which db/pipeline.ts:1273-1275 (listReconsiderQueue: 'Only entries carrying an auto_rejected event surface here') then routes into the Reconsider queue. The only legitimate senders are accepts: useSimulationEngine.ts:260 and useSimulationWalk.ts:575.

app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:128 seals `restoredStage: 'Screened'` literally, while db/pipeline.ts:1334 lands the entry on screenedLandingStage(getPipelineAxis(ws).stages) - a renamed column gets a sealed record naming a stage the candidate never stood on.

app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:126 seals rationale 'Auto-rejection reversed for re-review.' but db/pipeline.ts:1343 accepts ANY status='rejected' row, human rejects included (the reinstate door only checks status).

app/api/pipeline/batch/authz-parity.test.ts:33-42 hand-lists five GATED_ROUTES; rejected/route.ts, events/recent/route.ts, outcomes/route.ts, stage-impact/route.ts, stage-sla/route.ts, stage-migration/route.ts and command/reverse/route.ts are gated today but pinned by no family test.
rollback: Three commits (table+route, outcomes gate, tests/doc) revert cleanly: no schema, no catalog key, no store signature changes; runPipelineEntryAction and db/pipeline.ts are untouched (the claim is filtered at the route, the reinstate precondition reads listPipelineEventsForEntry). Reverting restores the two ALLOWED lines.
runner_up: One reversal door (L): reinstate, the command-wave undo and the re-add reopen share one planner + one sealed CAS restore - traded away because it must rewrite reinstatePipelineEntry in db/pipeline.ts, which r06 db-pipeline-store/A is building on right now.
body:
## Summary
The single-entry door POST /api/pipeline/[id] dispatches eight actions - reject with a candidate letter, accept that extends an offer, set_stage, reinstate and four field writes - behind requireOperator alone, the one pipeline write door besides outcomes that never asks the seat for pipeline:write. It also honours a body-supplied `actor:'sim'` on every action, so any operator can file a human rejection as a machine auto-reject. Turn the door into a declared action table (capability, engine-claim, reversal precondition per action), gate outcomes POST the same way, and derive the pipeline authz-parity pin from the directory instead of a five-route hand list.

## Description
The bulk doors (batch, command, reverse, stage-migration, stage-sla) all ask `requireCapabilityCoded('pipeline:write')`; the per-card door they were written to be in lock-step with does not (route-capability-coverage.test.ts:163 still lists it as 'not yet judged'). A viewer seat can therefore reject, advance, extend an offer or reverse a rejection one card at a time - exactly the class write-capability-gate.test.ts exists to refuse. The door's requirements live in four `if (body.action === ...)` branches plus a fall-through, so nothing states what each action needs; the registry's declarative-requirements technique says the requirement should be data adjacent to the operation, read by the one gate, with an undeclared operation unrepresentable. The same table carries the other two per-action facts the route gets wrong today: which action may carry an engine claim (only accept - the sim never sends it for anything else) and what a reinstate may reverse (only an auto-rejection, sealed with the stage the candidate actually landed on). Nothing in runPipelineEntryAction or db/pipeline.ts changes; both are in other in-flight write sets.

## Flow
1. entry-actions.ts: `ENTRY_ACTIONS = { set_github:{capability:'pipeline:write'}, ..., accept:{capability:'pipeline:write', engineClaim:true}, ... } as const`, a derived `EntryActionName` union and `entryActionOf(raw)` guard (the tabs.ts literal-array + union + guard shape).
2. route POST: requireOperator (unchanged, first) -> parse body -> entryActionOf -> 400 PIPELINE_ACTION_UNKNOWN when null -> requireCapabilityCoded(table[action].capability) -> dispatch. `actor` is forwarded only when `table[action].engineClaim`.
3. reinstate branch: read listPipelineEventsForEntry(id, 50, ws); refuse 409 PIPELINE_NOT_REINSTATABLE unless the newest decision event is auto_rejected; seal `restoredStage: restored.stage`.
4. outcomes POST: requireCapabilityCoded('pipeline:write') after requireOperator.
5. Tests: two DOORS rows + a set_notes/reinstate row in write-capability-gate.test.ts; delete the two ALLOWED lines; entry-actions.test.ts for the table; entry-route.test.ts for the claim + reinstate cases; authz-parity.test.ts walks the directory with a reasoned allowlist (events GET = public projection; pipeline/route.ts = debt, owned by r06 db-pipeline-store/A this wave).
6. docs/features/pipeline/README.md: the door's posture table and the engine-claim rule.

## Expected impact
Every pipeline write that can reach a candidate asks the seat; a viewer is refused with a coded 403 instead of silently rejecting. The decision chain can no longer carry a human's reject under 'auto:sim', so override rates and the Reconsider queue stop counting recruiter acts as machine acts, and every sealed reinstate names a real stage and reverses a real auto-rejection. A new action added to the door without a declared requirement fails typecheck, and a new pipeline route without a gate fails the derived parity test.

## Evaluation
Claim: every action on the pipeline entry and hire-rating write doors is gated by its declared seat capability, an engine claim survives only on accept, and a reinstate seals only a true reversal of an auto-rejection.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test under npm run test:unit (write-capability-gate.test.ts real handlers on unit-db, entry-actions.test.ts, entry-route.test.ts, authz-parity.test.ts, route-capability-coverage.test.ts), plus tsc and lint in the integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten.

title: Rate hires where the count is: Quality lists the unrated hires, rated in place
shared_surfaces: perf-budget.json (only if test:perf reports the Quality section graph grew)
acceptance: foldHireRatingQueue (pure): hires A (hiredAt 2026-05-01), B (2026-07-01), C (2026-08-01); latest outcomes {ref(A): outcome 'hired', performance 4} -> {hires:3, rated:1, unratedTotal:2, unrated:[B, C]} - oldest hire first, because the longest-serving hire is the one whose on-the-job outcome is knowable.

Same population, both halves: hires [A]; outcomes {X: 'hired', performance 5} where X is no current hire's ref (a dev-case-lane rating, or a hire since moved off the terminal column) -> rated 0, unrated [A]. (Today countRatedHires answers 1, so the Quality line reads '1 of 1 hires rated'.) Invariant over any input: rated <= hires.
An outcome on a hire's ref with performance null, or outcome other than 'hired' -> that hire stays in `unrated`; it never contributes a zero or counts as rated.

40 unrated hires -> unrated.length === QUEUE_CAP (25), unratedTotal 40; every row's keys are exactly {entryId, candidateLabel, jobTitle, hiredAt} - no score, no performance value, no contact, no workspace id.

listWorkspaceHires (unit-db): a workspace whose terminal-role column is renamed 'Joined' -> its entries on 'Joined' are hires and nothing on a column literally named 'Hired' elsewhere counts; another workspace's hire never appears; an entry with status 'declined' or 'rejected' standing on the terminal column is excluded; the read is not truncated by PIPELINE_BOARD_CAP.
GET /api/pipeline/outcomes with no ?entry returns {rated, hires, minOutcomes, unrated, unratedTotal}; GET ?entry=<id> returns the unchanged single-hire shape.
Rate from the queue: POST /api/pipeline/outcomes {entryId:B, performance:3} then GET -> B has left `unrated`, rated went 1 -> 2; re-rating A (performance 2) leaves rated at 2.

queueHeadline (pure view model): hires 0 -> 'none'; rated >= minOutcomes -> 'ready' with the queue still offered (collapsed); otherwise 'pending' with remaining = minOutcomes - rated - the three states the Quality copy already has, now computed off one fold.
premise: app/features/insights/analytics/sections/QualityInstrument.tsx:108 reads /api/pipeline/outcomes and :176-186 renders 'rated X of Y hires, N more needed' followed by messages/en.json:7663 hireRatingWhere: 'Ratings are recorded on a hired candidate, in the candidate panel on the hiring board.' - the surface states the gap and sends the reader away to close it one drawer at a time.

app/features/hiring/pipeline/candidate/CandidateOverviewTab.tsx:71 mounts PipelineHireOutcomeCard only inside one hired candidate's modal; there is no list of which hires are unrated anywhere in the app, so finding the N the counter asks for means opening every hire.

app/api/pipeline/outcomes/route.ts:83 `rated: countRatedHires(ws)` counts every dev_outcomes row with outcome 'hired' and performance set (app/_lib/dev-outcomes.ts:410-413), including /api/devcase/outcomes lane ratings and refs no longer on a terminal column, while :82 `hires` counts current terminal-role board entries - numerator and denominator are different populations, so 'X of Y' can overstate progress or exceed Y.

app/api/pipeline/outcomes/route.ts:82 counts hires by hydrating the whole board through listPipeline(ws) (db/pipeline.ts:790-791 -> listPipelinePage, capped at PIPELINE_BOARD_CAP = 2000, db/pipeline.ts:739) to keep a length.
The per-hire join already exists: dev-outcomes.ts:350-353 hireOutcomeRef(entry) and :540 latestOutcomeByRefs(refs, ws); outcomes/route.ts:63-64 uses exactly that pair for the single-hire read.

POST /api/pipeline/outcomes (route.ts:90-117) already validates entryId + performance with hirePerformanceSchema and re-checks the LIVE terminal stage (:106-110), so an in-place rating reuses the one write door the drawer uses.
rollback: Reverts cleanly as a commit series: the GET response only gains fields (unrated, unratedTotal), `rated` narrows to the hire set, the single-hire GET and the POST are unchanged, no schema or table is added (hire-roster.ts is a read over pipeline_entries), and the catalog keys are append-only.
runner_up: Reconsider from the rejected shelf: bring a hand-rejected candidate back onto the column they were rejected at, with 'the letter already went' stated - traded away because r06 db-pipeline-store/A makes the re-add the human reopen door, and the shelf UI should wait for that door to land rather than mint a second one.
body:
## Summary
Analytics -> Quality tells the reader 'rated 2 of 6 hires, 3 more needed before that curve could be judged', then sends them to the hiring board to open hired candidates one by one to find which four are unrated. Make the status actionable: the outcomes GET returns the unrated hires (oldest hire first, capped, label/role/hired-at only), the Quality verdict panel lists them with the same 1..5 rating control the drawer uses, and `rated` is computed over the same hire set as `hires` so the counter can no longer overstate itself.

## Description
The quality-of-hire question is the one the calibration page cannot answer without a human, and the app already has everything to make that human's job one screen: the hire roster (terminal-role entries), the per-hire outcome join (hireOutcomeRef + latestOutcomeByRefs, already used by the single-hire read), and a validated write door (POST /api/pipeline/outcomes, which re-checks the live stage). What is missing is the list. A pure fold, `foldHireRatingQueue(hires, latestByRef)`, returns {hires, rated, unratedTotal, unrated[]} with rated <= hires by construction - replacing countRatedHires, which counts dev-case-lane ratings and ex-hires into a numerator whose denominator is today's board. A targeted read (`listWorkspaceHires`, an uncapped SELECT on the workspace's terminal-role stage ids, in a route-local module so db/pipeline.ts - in r06 db-pipeline-store's write set - is untouched) replaces hydrating the whole board to count it. The queue rows carry no score and no rating value: the list is of people awaiting a judgement, never of judgements.

## Flow
1. hire-rating-queue.ts: QUEUE_CAP = 25; foldHireRatingQueue(hires, latestByRef) and queueHeadline({hires, rated, minOutcomes}) - pure, node:test first.
2. hire-roster.ts: listWorkspaceHires(ws, terminalStageIds) -> [{entryId, candidateId, devSubmissionId, candidateLabel, jobTitle, hiredAt: stage_changed_at}] for active (non-terminal-status) entries on a terminal-role column.
3. outcomes GET (no entry): roster -> refs via hireOutcomeRef -> latestOutcomeByRefs(refs, ws) -> fold -> {rated, hires, minOutcomes, unrated, unratedTotal}.
4. QualityHireRatingQueue.tsx: under the existing hireRating line, a PANEL list (name, role, 'hired N days ago', TOGGLE_GROUP 1..5 with the drawer's labels); a pick POSTs the existing door and re-reads the counter; refusal codes render through useErrorMessage; both themes via recipes/tokens only.
5. QualityInstrument.tsx: the line reads its three states from queueHeadline; hireRatingWhere becomes 'rate them here, or from the candidate panel'.
6. Four catalogs (queue heading, row age, empty/overflow 'and N more'), docs/features/analytics/README.md Quality section.

## Expected impact
The quality-of-hire curve stops waiting on a scavenger hunt: a hiring manager clears the rating backlog from the page that asks for it, in one sitting, and the counter they are clearing is true (rated is a subset of hires). The count read stops hydrating up to 2000 board rows per Quality view. No new write surface: the queue reuses the gated, stage-rechecking POST.

## Evaluation
Claim: the Quality tab lists every unrated current hire and rates it in place, and its 'X of Y rated' counts both halves over the same hire population.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test under npm run test:unit (hire-rating-queue.test.ts pure + unit-db roster and route round-trip), outcomes-route.test.ts source guards kept green, i18n:check and design:check in the integration gate; both themes checked on /?tab=analytics&sec=quality.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
